items.evidence: From work/ with no engine running, `python tools/kit.py build` exited 0 after about 29 s. It printed a JSON list of four entries with name, triangles, closed and bounds: gear_token 320, heart_pickup 1596, star_pickup 36, coin_pickup 576, all closed:true. The engine runs headless and the script stops it again.

`python tools/kit.py frames` exited 0 and rewrote frames/{gear_token,heart_pickup,star_pickup,coin_pickup}.png (timestamps 20:21). Each PNG header says 512x512. I opened all four: they are front views, and each prop is whole with a margin on every side.

The gear frame shows 12 identical teeth, evenly spaced, with one pointing straight up, and a round hole in the middle showing the background. My own reading of the exported glb found 24 tip vertices at 4.5+30k and 25.5+30k degrees (12 teeth exactly 30 degrees apart) and a smallest radius of 0.0300. A ray along z through the centre and at r=0.02 hits 0 triangles, so the hole goes right through.
Build bounds: x -0.1500..0.1500 (0.300), y 8e-7..0.3000 (0.300), z -0.025..0.025 (0.050). All are within 1% of the brief, and min y is 0.

The heart frame shows a clear heart: two round lobes on top, a point at the bottom, and shading at the rim. The exported mesh has 10 z-stations (+-0.025, 0.023, 0.020, 0.015, 0.009), so the edge is a stepped rounded profile, not a square one. It is faceted, but it is not sharp.

The star frame shows five sharp points, one pointing up. In the mesh the outline vertices alternate between radius 0.1577 and 0.0625 at 36-degree steps from 18 degrees, so the five tips are exactly 72 degrees apart. Bounds are x 0.300 wide and z 0.050 thick (0.315 measured tip-circle diameter).

Coin bounds: x -0.1..0.1 (0.2 across), z +-0.01 (0.02 thick), a full disc in the frame. Rays along z at r = 0, 0.05 and 0.08 meet the faces at z +-0.006, and at r = 0.09 and 0.095 at z +-0.01. So the rim, from r 0.085 to 0.1 (0.015 wide), stands 0.004 proud on both faces. The rim does not show in the head-on frame; I confirmed it from the geometry.

The build reported closed:true for all four. My own check welded points at 10 micrometres and found every undirected edge shared by exactly 2 triangles in all four meshes (0 bad edges), with positive volume. All four are single flat pieces upright on y=0, use the shared token_* materials of assets/style.json (style 'pickups'), and render in the same flat-token look.

README.md gives `python tools/kit.py build` and `python tools/kit.py frames`, run from work/. With no engine running, I ran both exactly as written. Both worked; each started the engine and stopped it again, and no game engine process was left afterwards.

defects: The README and style description say every token has a 'warm face colour', but the gear uses token_metal/steel (grey, #aeb8c4), which is not warm.
The coin's raised rim cannot be seen in its only frame (flat head-on lighting). The README admits this.
The star's points reach radius 0.1577, so its tip-circle diameter is 0.315. Only its x width is exactly 0.300; it is still about 0.3 across.
The build command writes .glb exports into assets/models/exports as a side effect of the watertight check.
